ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with a six-membered carbon ring above; it is connected to the fused bicyclic carbon skeleton below through the middle carbon labeled H. On the right, two C–N multiple-bond connections connected to nitrogen groups can be seen, one pointing to NH2+ and the other pointing to NH; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning count: Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms. The upper six-membered ring has 6 C–C bonds; the lower fused bicyclic carbon skeleton has 11 C–C bonds; the extra C–C connection from the upper ring to the center/lower skeleton is 1 bond; the two C–N connections on the right are 2 bonds. The C–H bond of the carbon labeled H is not counted, and any N–H bonds are also not counted. Therefore the total is 6 + 11 + 1 + 2 = 20.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows an upper six-membered ring attached through a central H-bearing carbon to a lower fused bicyclic carbon framework, plus two visible C–N multiple-bond connections to NH2+ and NH on the right.
